title: Phase stability, charge ordering, and charge-liquid formation in the Falicov-Kimball model on triangular and kagome lattices
abstract: We present a systematic investigation of the stability of the phase diagram of the spinless Falicov-Kimball model on two-dimensional non-bipartite lattices, the triangular and kagome lattices, using Markov-chain Monte Carlo simulations. Three filling or chemical potential conditions are examined: fixed chemical potentials ($μ_f = μ_c = U/2$), "generalized" half-filling ($\bar{n}_f = 1/3$, $\bar{n}_c = 2/3$), and conventional half-filling ($\bar{n}_f = \bar{n}_c = 1/2$). For each condition, the effects of a perturbatively small next-nearest-neighbor hopping are studied. On the triangular lattice, Anderson insulator, Mott insulator, and charge-density wave (CDW) phases are found in all cases, with the CDW driven by Coulomb-interaction-mediated nesting. Evidence for a charge-liquid regime is found in the region between the weakly correlated regime and the CDW, characterized by competing charge-ordering wavevectors and the absence of universal scaling behavior, whose extent shrinks progressively from the grand-canonical to the conventional half-filling condition. On the kagome lattice, the CDW phase is completely absent; instead, an insulating ground state, plausibly of the Mott type, is found, with signatures of a possible quantum phase transition at zero temperature. Our results establish the crucial role of lattice geometry and particle-hole symmetry breaking in shaping the phase diagram of correlated electron systems.
summary: This paper uses MCMC simulations to map the phase diagram of the Falicov-Kimball model on triangular and kagome lattices. It finds that lattice geometry is crucial, leading to distinct behaviors like CDW formation on the triangular lattice versus Mott-like insulation on the kagome lattice. The work highlights the complex interplay between correlation, geometry, and charge ordering in strongly correlated materials.
main_problem: The study systematically investigates the phase stability, charge ordering, and charge-liquid formation in the Falicov-Kimball model on two-dimensional non-bipartite lattices.
main_result: The lattice geometry critically dictates the phase diagram; the triangular lattice exhibits CDW phases, while the kagome lattice shows an insulating ground state without CDW ordering.
method: The research employs Markov-chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) simulations to analyze the system's behavior under various filling conditions and hopping perturbations.
model_or_system: The system is the spinless Falicov-Kimball model, describing itinerant ($c$) and localized ($f$) fermions interacting via a Coulomb repulsion ($U$) on triangular and kagome lattices.
key_observables: Specific heat capacity ($c_v(T)$), charge susceptibilities ($\chi(q, T)$), gap ($\Delta$), and Inverse Participation Ratio (IPR).
important_parameters: Coulomb interaction strength ($U$), lattice geometry (triangular vs. kagome), and filling conditions (fixed chemical potentials, generalized/conventional half-filling).
main_assumptions: The analysis probes stability across different ensembles (grand-canonical vs. canonical) and assumes the effect of perturbatively small next-nearest-neighbor hopping ($t_{NNN}$).
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the finite-sized triangular and kagome lattices used for the simulations.
paper_structure: The paper systematically examines the phase diagram by testing three different filling conditions on both the triangular and kagome lattices, analyzing the emergence of CDW, Mott, and charge-liquid regimes.
why_interesting: The study provides detailed insights into how lattice topology (non-bipartite geometry) and particle-hole symmetry breaking fundamentally alter the ground state and phase transitions in correlated electron models.

figures.caption: Figure 1: Illustration of finite-sized triangular (left) and kagome (right) lattices. The light-blue hexagon indicates the conventional unit cell.

Figure 2: Phase diagram of the triangular lattice for FCP, CHF, and GHF cases as mentioned in the text, at vanishing next-nearest-neighbor hopping, tNNN = 0. The region U/t < 1 is grayed out due to restrictions of the applied methods. The colored shaded regions mark the charge-liquid sector, i.e. the non-universal regime that precedes the onset of long-range CDW order, where several ordering wavevectors compete with each other.

Figure 3: Specific heat cv(T), c-DoS ρc(EF , T), c-electron gap ∆(EF , T), and IPR(EF , T) for the FCP case on the triangular lattice. For clarity, curves corresponding to larger U are vertically offset relative to the preceding one, where respective individual baselines are drawn for each curve.
